name: Veg Fried Rice

ingredients.name: Spring onion (hara pyaz)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 2 stalks; whites chopped separately from the greens

ingredients.name: Black pepper powder (kali mirch) (or white pepper)
Salt
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅛ tsp (adjust; soy sauce is already salty)

equipment: Chopping board and a sharp knife
Small bowls to keep each chopped vegetable ready (stir-frying is fast, so everything must be chopped before the flame goes on)
Measuring spoons and a measuring cup
Plate for cooling the rice if it is freshly cooked

steps.text: Break up the rice gently with your fingers so the grains separate

steps.title: Add the diced onion and the spring onion whites, and stir-fry

steps.title: Add the carrot and beans, and stir-fry on high heat

steps.title: Add the cabbage and capsicum, and stir-fry
steps.text: Add the cabbage and capsicum, and stir-fry

steps.title: Add the loosened rice to the wok

steps.cameraCheck: the rice on top of the vegetables

steps.title: Toss and fold the rice with the vegetables on high heat, spreading it out and pressing any lumps
steps.text: Toss and fold the rice with the vegetables on high heat, spreading it out and pressing any lumps

reasons: the home version uses only 2 tsp oil, about 175 g of mixed vegetables and moderate soy sauce, with no frying beyond a quick stir-fry. It is still mainly refined white rice with only about 8 g protein, so it is filling but not balanced on its own. Restaurant and street versions typically use 2–3 tbsp oil, often add MSG (ajinomoto), use much more soy sauce and salt (often well over 1.5 g sodium), and contain far fewer vegetables relative to rice.

researchRating.basis: veg fried rice is one of the most-ordered and most-cooked Indo-Chinese dishes in India. Top recipe pages have near-perfect ratings from hundreds of readers, and comments often call it a quick, reliable way to use leftover rice. It loses a little because many people see it as a side for Manchurian or chilli dishes rather than a standout dish on its own, and home versions are often described as "not as smoky as the restaurant".

storage: Fridge: cool it quickly (within 1 hour of cooking) and keep it in an airtight container for up to 1 day, at most 2. Cooked rice left at room temperature can grow *Bacillus cereus*, so do not leave it out for long. Freezer: possible for up to 1 month in a flat freezer bag, though the vegetables lose some crunch. Reheating: stir-fry in a hot pan with 1 tsp water or oil for 2–3 minutes until steaming hot all the way through, or microwave covered with a sprinkle of water for 1.5–2 min, stirring halfway. Reheat only once.
leftoverRemix: make fried-rice "Schezwan arancini" (rice tikkis). Mash about 1 cup leftover fried rice with 2 tbsp grated paneer, 1 tbsp cornflour and ½ tsp Schezwan sauce, shape into small balls or patties, and shallow-fry or air-fry until crisp. Serve with ketchup or mint chutney.
burnOff: Running: about 5.6 km at about 70 kcal per km. Walking: about 8 km at a brisk pace (est.), using about 50 kcal per km.
